nodes.name: Electrochemical degreasing
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, the substrates were degreased by anodically polarizing them for 5 min at 5 V (vs. a large nickel counter electrode) in an aqueous solution of 55.5 g/L NaOH and 14.0 g/L Na2SiO3.
nodes.source_text: Subsequently, the substrates were degreased by anodically polarizing them for 5 min at 5 V (vs. a large nickel counter electrode) in an aqueous solution of 55.5 g/L NaOH and 14.0 g/L Na2SiO3.

nodes.name: Acid pickling
nodes.procedure: The remaining surface oxides were removed by submerging the substrates in an acidic pickling solution, consisting of 110 g/L Metex M629, for 5 min.
nodes.source_text: The remaining surface oxides were removed by submerging the substrates in an acidic pickling solution, consisting of 110 g/L Metex M629, for 5 min.

nodes.name: KOH solution preparation
nodes.procedure: The potassium hydroxide (KOH) solution was prepared by dissolving pellets in Milli-Q water. The solution was preelectrolyzed for 1 week using HCl-cleaned nickel mesh electrodes, and the purity of the final solution was checked by Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectrometry (ICP-OES) (Table S1).
nodes.source_text: The potassium hydroxide (KOH) solution was prepared by dissolving pellets in Milli-Q water. The solution was preelectrolyzed for 1 week using HCl-cleaned nickel mesh electrodes...

nodes.name: Iron-free KOH preparation
nodes.procedure: Extra pure, iron-free KOH was prepared by adding Ni(OH)2 powder to the preelectrolyzed KOH and subsequently filtering the solution, a method adapted from Trotochaud et al.

nodes.description: Custom intermittent redox cycling parameter study - shutdown cycles effect
nodes.source_text: a representative case of operation at 80 °C with 120 shutdown cycles of 1 h duration resulted in ∼0.3% mass loss, equivalent to 0.42 mg Ni/cm² for a flat surface. Accounting for the mesh structure (1.66 × geometric area...), this equates to 0.25 mg Ni/cm_ECSA², corresponding to a thickness of ∼0.28 μm

nodes.source_text: Temperature also exerts a strong influence, with mass loss rising significantly between 80 °C and 110 °C. As shown in Fig. 6c, the data do not follow a simple Arrhenius-type relationship

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS validates cleanliness of pretreated nickel 201 electrodes (Fig. S1) and depth profiling shows 4–10 at.% Fe (relative to Ni) throughout electrochemically grown hydroxide surface layers of O2 electrodes exposed to 1.5 mg/L Fe electrolyte (Fig. S15).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The cleanliness of the pretreated electrodes was validated using XPS (Fig. S1). ... XPS depth profiling, using Ar+ sputtering, revealed that 4–10 at.% Fe (relative to Ni) is present at the outermost surface layer in O2 electrodes with 1.5 mg Fe/L in the electrolyte (Fig. S15).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows changes in surface morphology of nickel O2 electrodes after shutdowns involving reverse currents, with substantially altered microstructure for electrodes suffering considerable mass loss.
nodes.evidence_snippet: shutdowns involving reverse currents led to 0.16–2.05% mass loss, accompanied by changes in surface morphology as observed by SEM (Fig. S9). ... electrodes that suffered a considerable mass loss revealed a substantially altered microstructure when analyzed by SEM (Fig. S12).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ Raman shows that only O2 electrodes operated with limited amounts of reverse currents during shutdown contained substantial amounts of NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ex situ Raman spectroscopy similarly showed that only O2 electrodes operated with limited amounts of reverse currents during shutdown contained substantial amounts of NiOOH (Fig. S23).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms no iron signal in iron-free KOH and measures nickel content in electrolyte matching electrode mass loss when stirred, with decreasing iron levels over time.
nodes.evidence_snippet: No iron signal could be detected in the ICP-OES spectra from these samples. ... The nickel content measured by ICP-OES was, however, consistently much lower than the combined electrode mass loss unless the electrolyte was thoroughly stirred before sample extraction.
